newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Citystate buys insurance units, expansion planned.
newsitem.headline: Citystate buys insurance units, expansion planned.

text.p: Insurance group Citystate Holdings Pte Ltd (CHPL) said on Thursday it had made acquisitions in Hong Kong and Singapore as part of its strategic expansion plan in Asia.
CHPL said in a statement the most significant deal was taking a Singapore $4.5 million controlling 55 percent stake in Hong Kong-based Pan South Insurance Company Ltd (PSI).
CHPL chairman Leow Siak Fah said in the statement the deal created synergies for the two firms and would give CHPL a springboard into China.
PSI had gross written premium of Hong Kong $13 million (S$2.3 million) in the nine months to December 31 1996 and made pre-tax profit of HK$2.6 million.
Leow said CHPL was also expanding its broking interests, an area where it saw much growth potential.

CHPL paid S$317,000 for a 55 percent controlling interest in Hong Kong insurance broker Stenhouse South China Ltd and S$750,000 for 100 percent of the equity of Singapore broker and consultancy, Newstate Associates Pte Ltd.
The acquisitions took place between September and December 1996, the statement said.
